prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the camera wearer walking forward along an indoor corridor flanked by close walls (0.5–1.5 m) on the left and right before turning right into a glass-enclosed shop aisle with shelving units in frames 4 and 5. In frames 1 and 2, a person in front to the right (~1.5–2 m away, occluded in frame 2) and another standing by a left counter (~3–4 m away, moving to ~2–2.5 m in frame 2) are clearly separated in depth from the dark background hallway (~8–10 m away), while in frames 3 to 5 a person with long hair walks directly ahead within 0.5–1.2 m (arm's reach) of the camera wearer and shifts to the right in frame 5 as a snack shelf enters within 0.5–1 m on the left. All visible people face away from or perpendicular to the camera wearer and never look toward the viewpoint, with their lower bodies cropped at the bottom of the frame and the foreground person in frame 3 partially occluding a person just behind and to the left (~1.5 m away). Compared to RGB alone, the depth gradient makes the continuous distance to featureless white walls, the receding floor plane, and the close proximity of the shelving units in frames 4 and 5 immediately quantifiable. However, the map is unreliable on transparent and reflective glass partitions in frames 1, 4, and 5—rendering the glass door frame as an opaque solid barrier while losing background depth cues beyond the upper shelving.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete people and select background objects across the corridor and store entrance, tracking two people in the lower left and center-left in frame 1 (~2 m and ~3.5 m away, separated by ~1.5 m) and a person standing on the left (~2.5 m away) alongside a distant potted plant (~9 m away) and another shopper (~7 m away on the right) in frame 2. In frames 3 through 5, a large pink mask tracks the person directly in front of the camera wearer (~0.5–1.2 m away, within arm's reach, moving to the right edge in frame 5), showing them occluding a second person immediately to their left in frame 3 (~1.5 m away) and partially occluding the potted plant (~6 m away on the left) and two distant people (~5–7 m away behind the shelves) in frame 4. Combined with the RGB strip, we see that the foreground person faces forward away from the camera wearer throughout frames 3–5, the person on the left in frames 1–2 faces the left counter with a bag and counter within their arm's reach, and the distant people in frames 2 and 4 face the right-side shelves. This map highlights distant, heavily occluded individuals behind the store shelving in frame 4 and the shopper next to the potted plant in frame 2 that are hard to spot at a glance in the RGB image. However, the segmentation is highly unreliable in frame 4 where a massive false-positive 'refrigerator' mask covers the entire upper-right room, ceiling, and shelving, and across all frames it completely misses the counters, walls, and the close-up snack rack on the left in frame 5 (which is within 0.5–1 m of the camera wearer).
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost completely blank across all five frames, failing to detect any body or hand skeletons for the people walking in the hallway or browsing the store shelves. The only rendered feature appears near the top-center of frame 1 as a small cluster of magenta hand keypoints extending downward from the upper edge, located roughly where a ceiling-mounted light fixture and wall frame meet (~2–3 m above and in front of the camera wearer). From the RGB context, multiple people are actually present from 0.5 m (within arm's reach in frames 3–5) to 7 m away, facing away from or sideways to the camera wearer with their lower bodies or torsos occluded by the frame boundary, counters, and each other as the camera wearer walks forward and turns into the aisle. Because no valid human skeletons are extracted, this map provides no additional spatial insight beyond RGB and is completely unreliable here—producing a false-positive hand skeleton on ceiling architecture in frame 1 while missing every actual person and hand in the scene due to rear-facing views, motion blur, and severe lower-body cropping.
